episode_title: Transfix Take Podcast | Week of Oct 20 - Flat Rates, Rising Risk: Freight's Cross-Border Capacity Squeeze

real_qa.q: What is C.H. Robinson's legal strategy regarding the Texas motor carrier classification case?
real_qa.r: As of October 19th, C.H. Robinson released statements confirming that it will appeal the judgment to the Texas Court of Appeals, maintaining that the motor carrier was independent. This case involved holding a broker vicariously liable for an FMCSA authorized entity, which was a major development in freight contracting law.
real_qa.requete: C.H. Robinson Texas Court of Appeals motor carrier

real_qa.q: How did the revocation of Mexican driver visas impact U.S.-Mexico cross-border freight rates?
real_qa.r: The U.S.-Mexico border experienced a huge capacity shock over the weekend with a revocation of about 25,000 Mexican driver visas for broker enforcement and tender rejections. This spike significantly impacted spot rates for U.S. to Mexico cross-border freight, creating capacity constraints.
real_qa.requete: Mexican driver visas revocation cross-border freight rates

real_qa.q: What is the current national average diesel fuel price and line haul rate per mile as of October 2024?
real_qa.r: As of October 20th, the national average diesel price was $6.27, down two cents from the previous week. The national average line haul rate per mile was $2.22, which had been relatively flat since the first week of October, with tender rejections holding steady at 12.7%.
real_qa.requete: diesel price October 2024 line haul rate per mile

real_qa.q: Which West Coast markets are showing the strongest freight rate increases heading into November?
real_qa.r: Los Angeles and Ontario, the mega markets on the West Coast, are seeing increases of 2%, and compared to 30 days ago, freight leaving the West Coast is up 7%. Portland in the Pacific Northwest has seen increases of about 5% in just the past week, driven by peak produce season and Christmas tree season demand.
real_qa.requete: West Coast freight rates Los Angeles Portland October 2024

real_qa.q: What regulatory changes are driving freight industry capacity constraints through 2027 and 2028?
real_qa.r: The industry has faced compiling regulatory pressures including English language proficiency requirements, cracking down on chameleon carriers and CDL mills, non-domicile issues, and major changes from the Montgomery versus Caravee case. The landscape is expected to look different throughout 2027 and 2028, driving the capacity constraints discussed over the past couple of months.
real_qa.requete: Montgomery versus Caravee freight carrier regulation 2027
